# MCP Integrations

Connect your application or agent to a [Model Context Protocol (MCP)](https://vercel.com/docs/mcp) server to use its tools. Choose an integration based on how you build your agent:

| Integration | Use it when | Connection setup |
|---|---|---|
| [eve](https://vercel.com/docs/mcp/integrations/eve) | You build durable backend agents with eve. | Define a connection under `agent/connections/` and configure authentication. |
| [AI SDK](https://vercel.com/docs/mcp/integrations/ai-sdk) | You build agents and model calls with the AI SDK. | Create an MCP client and pass its tools to the model. |
| [TanStack AI](https://vercel.com/docs/mcp/integrations/tanstack-ai) | You use TanStack AI's chat and streaming APIs. | Pass an MCP client to `chat()` for managed tool discovery and cleanup. |

The AI SDK and TanStack AI examples connect to a server hosted on Vercel and send model requests through [AI Gateway](https://vercel.com/docs/ai-gateway). The eve guide connects to an OAuth-protected MCP server through [Vercel Connect](https://vercel.com/docs/connect).

Each integration needs the MCP server's endpoint and any credentials that server requires. Model credentials and MCP credentials authenticate separate requests.

For OAuth-protected servers, see the Vercel Connect guides for [AI SDK](https://vercel.com/docs/connect/frameworks/ai-sdk-and-mcp) and [eve](https://vercel.com/docs/connect/frameworks/eve#authorize-an-mcp-connection).

- [Deploy an MCP server on Vercel](https://vercel.com/docs/mcp/deploy-mcp-servers-to-vercel) to expose your application's tools.
- [Use Vercel's MCP server](https://vercel.com/docs/agent-resources/vercel-mcp) to work with Vercel projects, deployments, and documentation.

Last updated September 15, 2026
